# DataWeave operator and function behavior

Reference for [the DataWeave rules](../../../instructions/dataweave.instructions.md). Read it before using the operators and functions below. Items marked (documented) are stated in MuleSoft documentation; items marked (CLI) were observed with the DataWeave CLI (runtime 2.12.2, language levels 2.4–2.9) and should be confirmed on the project's runtime when they decide the outcome.

- `isBlank` and `trim` treat every character from U+0000 to U+0020 as blank, but not U+007F, U+00A0 (no-break space), U+2003 or U+3000 (CLI). When the contract defines which characters count as blank, check exactly those. `upper` can change length (`"straße"` gives `"STRASSE"`), and precomposed and combining forms of a character are not equal (CLI).
- `-` removes by value, not by position: `[1,2,3] - 2` gives `[1,3]` (documented). It removed every occurrence (`["a","b","a"] - "a"` gave `["b"]`), and removing a value that is not there changed nothing, with no error (CLI). `obj - "key"` removes every key with that name (CLI). To remove several values or keys, or one specific key and value, use `--` (`{hello: "world", name: "DW"} -- {hello: "world"}` gives `{name: "DW"}`, documented); `obj - {k: v}` does not compile (CLI). See [operators](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-operators) and [`--`](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-core-functions-minusminus).
- When the array size can vary, use `take`, `drop` and `slice` from `dw::core::Arrays`, which stay within the array: `take` returns `[]` when `n <= 0` and the whole array when `n` exceeds its size; `drop` returns the whole array when `n <= 0` and `[]` when `n` exceeds its size; `slice` starts at the first item for a negative start, stops at the last item for an end past it, and returns `[]` for an end below the first index, so `slice(arr, 1, -1)` is `[]` (documented). Range selectors instead returned `null` when the range ran past the end or the array was empty (`arr[3 to 10]` on six items, `[][0 to -1]`) (CLI), and a reversed range returns items in reverse order (`[0,1,2][-1 to 0]` gives `[2,1,0]`, documented). See [take](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-arrays-functions-take), [drop](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-arrays-functions-drop), [slice](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-arrays-functions-slice) and the [range selector](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-cookbook-extract-data#range).
- To change one nested value, use the `update` operator (`payload update { case .a.b -> v }`): `!` after the path creates a missing field, an `if` makes the change conditional, and without `!` a missing path is left unchanged with no error. A path matches only the first of repeated keys or XML elements; put `*` on the repeating step (`.root.numbers.*number.@parity`) to change them all (CLI). See [update operator](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-operators).
- For structure-wide changes, consider `mask` from `dw::util::Values`, and `mapLeafValues` and `filterTree` from `dw::util::Tree`. `payload mask "password" with "*****"` masks matching leaf values at every depth, but leaves object- or array-valued password fields intact (CLI). Validate the shape or explicitly remove/replace the whole sensitive field before logging. See [mask](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-values-functions-mask). On very large payloads a plain recursive `map`/`mapObject` walk was about twice as fast (20,000 records: 0.33 s against 0.77 s), so measure before swapping one for the other.
- Non-tail recursion fails with `Stack Overflow. Max stack is 256` (CLI: 250 levels passed, 256 failed). For long or deep input, prefer built-ins or make the recursive call the last operation and mark the function `@TailRec()`, which rejects a function that is not tail recursive (CLI: tail recursion ran 100,000 levels). Do not raise `com.mulesoft.dw.stacksize` for one script; it applies to the whole runtime. See [troubleshooting](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-troubleshoot) and [annotations](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-core-annotations).
